title: How Names Can Tell Painful Stories

blanks.section: A name inherited through religion and empire

blanks.sentence: The missionary after whom the bishop was named set up several _____ in South India.
blanks.section: A name inherited through religion and empire

blanks.sentence: Despite his good aims, his _____ with colonial rulers gives the name a difficult history.
blanks.section: A name inherited through religion and empire

blanks.sentence: Names in India can indicate a person's _____.
blanks.section: A name inherited through religion and empire

blanks.sentence: Conversion to Christianity and new names gave some families greater _____ from social discrimination.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast about personal names introduces the discussion?
options: They shape how people see themselves, although parents usually choose them.
They matter mainly in childhood, although adults continue to use them.
They reflect family history, although most people select them as adults.
They express religious beliefs, although families may later reject them.

multipleChoice.question: How does the discussion broaden the reasons for changing a birth name?
options: It shifts from cultural pronunciation to difficulties with legal records.
It shifts from simple dislike to painful connections with past unfairness.
It shifts from family pressure to a desire for religious recognition.
It shifts from social standing to a preference for shorter names.

multipleChoice.question: What makes the missionary's legacy difficult for the bishop to carry?
options: His schools were opened only after colonial rule ended.
His religious aims prevented him from helping local children.
His family name was adopted without the bishop's knowledge.
His educational work was tied to support for colonial power.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred about discussing the British Empire's role in India?
options: Family names provide a complete record of colonial events.
The missionaries' schools settle the question of the empire's value.
A fair assessment should consider both educational work and colonial harm.
The empire's influence ended when people changed religion.

multipleChoice.question: How did taking Christian names help some low-status Indians?
options: It made their original names easier for others to pronounce.
It allowed them to claim a higher position within the empire.
It offered a way to avoid discrimination linked to social status.
It preserved the names used by earlier generations of their family.

multipleChoice.question: What broader point does the Beckford surname illustrate?
options: A surname can reveal exactly where an ancestor was born.
A surname can show whether a person shares an ancestor's beliefs.
A surname can lose its historical meaning within one generation.
A surname can carry a painful past into later generations.

multipleChoice.question: What quality in biblical figures influenced the name chosen for the professor's son?
options: Their readiness to confront injustice and powerful people.
Their success in gaining authority within government.
Their ability to avoid upsetting people with different views.
Their willingness to leave their inherited names behind.

multipleChoice.question: What might the final reflection imply for someone who keeps a name with a painful history?
options: Its religious origin determines how others will judge the person.
The person may still give the name significance through their actions.
Its historical meaning should always lead to a change.
The person's family must decide how the name is used.
